title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A is a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field K of characteristic 0 and residue field k of characteristic p>0. E_K is an elliptic curve over K. The object of study is the p-adic Tate module T_p(E_{\bar K}), a free Z_p-module of rank 2 with an action of Gal(\bar K/K). The bracketed remark seems to say that T_p over \bar K agrees with T_p over the algebraic closure of the completion. The aim, announced as 'étude infinitésimale', is to classify the possible structures of this Galois module according to the reduction type.

Case (a): good ordinary reduction. E_K extends to an elliptic scheme E/A and E_k is ordinary. The connected–étale sequence of the p-divisible group E[p^∞] over A gives a canonical exact sequence of Galois modules:
0 → L^∨(1) → T_p(E_{\bar K}) → L → 0.
Here L = T_p(E_k) is étale of rank 1 and unramified. The sub is the Cartier dual twist L^∨ ⊗ T_p(G_m), written L^∨[1]; it is the Tate module of the multiplicative-type formal group. This uses the Weil pairing / self-duality of E.

The extension class lies in Ext^1(L, L^∨(1)) = H^1(K, L^{-2} ⊗ Z_p(1)). Assume the residue field is algebraically closed, or pass to the strict henselization or maximal unramified extension. Then L becomes trivial, L ≅ L_0 ⊗ Z_p with L_0 its value over k. Kummer theory gives
H^1(K, Z_p(1)) ⊗ L_0^{-2} ≅ (lim K^*/K^{*p^n}) ⊗ L_0^{-2} ≅ Hom(L_0^{⊗2}, \widehat{K^*}).
The next page adds that the class actually lies in the subgroup Hom(L_0^{⊗2}, 1+m_A) of principal units ('Einseinheiten'), calling this 'bien connu'. A margin note says the extension can be split, which is the canonical (CM) lift.

This is precisely the Serre–Tate parameter q(E) ∈ Hom(T_pE_k ⊗ T_pE_k^t, \hat G_m(A)) of an ordinary elliptic curve. Here T_pE_k^t is identified with T_pE_k by the principal polarization, hence L_0^{⊗2}. The next page then treats the supersingular ('hypersingulière') case, conjecturing that the image of π_1(K) in Aut(T_p) is either small or open, and the potentially good reduction case.
errors: No substantive mathematical error. The twist bookkeeping is right: Ext^1(L, L^∨(1)) = H^1(K, L^{-2}(1)). Kummer theory is applied correctly.
Minor notational looseness: T_p(E_K) is written where the Galois module T_p(E_{\bar K}) is meant. L^∨[1] is Grothendieck's notation for the Tate twist (1).

The passage from H^1(K, L^{-2}(1)) to Hom(L_0^2, \hat K^*) presupposes L trivial. This is legitimate only after base change to an algebraically closed residue field, or the strict henselization, as he indicates. Over a general k one must take Galois-invariants, and this step is left implicit.

ideas.what: Canonical connected-étale extension 0→L^∨(1)→T_p(E)→L→0 for good ordinary reduction, with L unramified of rank 1
ideas.modern_name: Connected–étale (ordinary) filtration of the p-adic Tate module / p-divisible group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (p-divisible groups, 1966); Serre, Abelian l-adic representations (1968)
ideas.where_published: Standard. Appears in Tate's Driebergen paper and in Serre's book, which Grothendieck cites on the previous page.

ideas.what: Extension class identified via Kummer theory with Hom(L_0^{⊗2}, \hat K^*), in fact with values in principal units (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate canonical coordinates / Serre–Tate q-parameter of ordinary local moduli
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate (Woods Hole 1964 / Lubin–Serre–Tate); Messing (1972); Katz, 'Serre–Tate local moduli' (1981)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts, though related deformation theory of p-divisible groups appears in his 1970 Nice talk and in the Montréal 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974).

ideas.what: Possibility that the ordinary extension splits (canonical lift / CM)
ideas.modern_name: Canonical (quasi-canonical) lift, split Tate module in the CM case
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate; Serre (1968) for the Galois-theoretic statement

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean private rederivation of Serre–Tate theory for ordinary elliptic curves over p-adic fields: the canonical extension and its Kummer class in Hom(T⊗T, \hat G_m). Grothendieck himself calls the key fact 'bien connu'. It is historically nice as evidence of his working through Serre's 1968 book in the crystalline period, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'T_p(E_K) est de rang 2' should read T_p(E_{\bar K}) (bar over K is visible).
The bracketed addition near item 1° reads approximately '[et T_p(E_{\bar K}) = T_p(E_{\bar{\hat K}})]', i.e. a comparison with the completion rather than a tautology.

'A est à corps résiduel alg. clos' is rendered in the image as 'A est à corps résiduel alg. clos (dans le [?] sur A) résiduellement...'; the insertion likely refers to replacing A by its strict henselization or maximal unramified extension.
Final line: '≃ Hom(L_0^2, \widehat{K^*})' — hat over K^* confirmed. Under the Kummer group the annotation reads 'Z_p' with 'les valeurs en k', apparently explaining that L_0 is the value of L over k.
